newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka suspends plan to build government complex.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka suspends plan to build government complex.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has ordered an immediate halt to the construction of a new complex that would have housed her residence and other offices, state radio said on Wednesday.

The radio said Kumaratunga, who is travelling overseas, had advised her officials to stop work on the new 1.5 billion rupee ($25.8 million) complex after people in the area protested that they would lose their homes.
"The directive was issued after taking into account views put forward by various people," the radio quoted a senior official from Kumaratunga's secretariat as saying.

The goverment had planned to shift all government administrative establishments, defence headquarters and the official residence of the head of state to Sri Jayawardenapura Kotte, a suburb of the capital Colombo.
The goverment moved the parliament from central Colombo to Sri Jayawardenapura in 1982.

Preliminary work such as land surveying and security consultations had already begun and residents in the area said they had been advised by authorities that they would be compensated for the loss of their homes.

Housing Minister Indika Gunewardena earlier told parliament that moving the defence ministry alone would have freed some 80 acres of prime land in central Colombo with a commercial value of some 25 billion rupees ($431 million).
Moving other offices would free additional land valued at 1.2 billion rupees for commercial development.
Gunewardena said shifting Kumaratunga's residence to a suburb would also save the public the inconvenience of closed roads due to the president's security requirements.
"Furthermore, present restrictions in Colombo will adversly affect future investment in the city," he said.
Road blocks and military checkpoints are common in Colombo. Security is tight because of threats to political leaders by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The LTTE are waging a 14-year-old war against government troops for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
